It also contains no case-specific evidence about pair_A/pair_B springs or L=6.3 cm.","quote":"a specified displacement-controlled load is applied along the negative y-axis on the top surface"},{"source_id":"K5ba21260fb623147","relation":"irrelevant","reason":"Discusses geometrically nonlinear equilibrium paths and uses the current stiffness parameter to locate limit points, but does not derive the needed spring-loaded displacement-control criterion or state whether the critical loading/negative stiffness ratio is 1 or an O(1) geometric factor. It does not address play/stop coarse-graining.","quote":"It is seen that at the extreme points of the load–displacement curve CSP has the value zero. In this situation, the incremental stiffness matrix K T is singular."},{"source_id":"Ke929929c7a6d22d6","relation":"irrelevant","reason":"Abstract concerns electrostatic fixed-load snap-through/pull-in of arch beams; it does not provide the finite-stiffness-spring displacement-control limit-point criterion or stiffness-ratio condition, and does not discuss play/stop operators.","quote":"The snap-through occurs by exerting a fixed load, and the structure experiences a discontinuous displacement jump without consuming power."},{"source_id":"K59d96b908b49c9d1","relation":"irrelevant","reason":"Abstract mentions the classical Preisach model as a superposition of relay operators, but supplies no formal statement about coarse-graining play/stop operators to ±1 outputs or preservation of wiping-out and congruency. It also does not address the snap-through loading-stiffness criterion.","quote":"An emphasis is made on the classical Preisach model of hysteresis, which is a weighted superposition of relay operators."},{"source_id":"K5505bed0b02387a3","relation":"irrelevant","reason":"Concerns random-field Ising-model hysteresis and avalanche critical scaling, not Preisach/play operator wiping-out or congruency under discrete coarse-graining, nor spring-loaded snap-through limit-point criteria.","quote":"We have studied the nonequilibrium zero-temperature random-field Ising-model as a model for hysteretic behavior at first-order phase transformations."}],"revised_queries":["spring-loaded snap-through critical stiffness","discrete Preisach operator wiping-out congruency"]},{"assessments":[{"source_id":"Kd07e02313e0ce192","relation":"irrelevant","reason":"Discusses QZS metastructure and negative stiffness from snap-through, but gives no finite-spring displacement-control limit-point criterion, no critical loading/negative stiffness ratio, and no play/stop coarse-graining statement. It also contains no pair_A/pair_B spring or L=6.3 cm evidence.","quote":"the inclined beams exhibit buckling and snap-through behavior, contributing negative stiffness, while the semicircular arches provide positive stiffness through bending-dominated behavior."},{"source_id":"Ke4a32fd4fc008366","relation":"irrelevant","reason":"Uses displacement-driven loading and equilibrium/bifurcation paths for snap-through cells, but does not state the explicit finite-loading-spring limit-point criterion or whether the critical stiffness ratio is 1 or an O(1) geometric factor. It does not address play/stop operators.","quote":"A displacement-driven load is applied at the left end-node"},{"source_id":"Kd2a532e9a1eb6c57","relation":"irrelevant","reason":"Concerns viscoelastic snap-through dynamics and pseudo-bistability, not a finite-stiffness spring loading criterion or play/stop operator preservation of wiping-out and congruency.","quote":"two types of snap-through are possible: the truss either immediately snaps back over the elastic timescale or it displays ‘pseudo-bistability’"},{"source_id":"K1364a25c430600ea","relation":"irrelevant","reason":"States that play/Preisach models share wiping-out and congruency properties, but does not formally address coarse-graining play/stop operators to ±1 outputs or preservation of those properties under such coarse-graining. It also gives no spring-loaded snap-through criterion.","quote":"The models share several mathematical properties, such as the congruency property and wiping-out property"},{"source_id":"K7c34157152280fec","relation":"irrelevant","reason":"Describes KP/Preisach hysteresis and requires wiping-out and congruency, but does not provide the needed formal statement for play/stop operators after coarse-graining to ±1 outputs, nor any finite-spring snap-through limit-point criterion.","quote":"In order to be able to use the KP model to model a process hysteresis, hysteresis has to satisfy two properties: the wiping-out property and the congruency property."},{"source_id":"K66a33a03c6e99e71","relation":"irrelevant","reason":"Closest to the hysteresis sub-gap because it asserts a modified inverted switch operator retains wiping-out and congruency, but it is an inverted Preisach switch model, not a formal treatment of play/stop coarse-graining to ±1 outputs, and it gives no spring-loading limit-point criterion.","quote":"By applying this inverted switch operator, the inverted model retains the wiping-out and congruency properties."},{"source_id":"K3f6699082630dceb","relation":"irrelevant","reason":"Duplicate review abstract noting general play/Preisach properties but not the specific coarse-graining-to-±1 preservation statement and not the finite-spring snap-through limit-point criterion.","quote":"The models share several mathematical properties, such as the congruency property and wiping-out property"}],"revised_queries":["finite-stiffness spring loading limit-point criterion","Prandtl-Ishlinskii play operator memory properties"]},{"assessments":[{"source_id":"Kd81b72e9f33cf252","relation":"irrelevant","reason":"Granular/three-body contact mechanics of a wet coal-dust layer: defines a force-chain identification criterion (contact-force, particle-size, length, angle thresholds) and a DEM-FEM contact-stiffness calibration. It contains no limit-point/snap-through criterion for a finite-stiffness loading spring (no statement whether the critical loading-stiffness/negative-stiffness ratio is 1 or carries an O(1) geometric factor), and no play/stop operator theory. It also reports no case-specific pair_A/pair_B spring (k≈0.19 N/cm) or L=6.3 cm installation data.","quote":"Based on the bearing characteristics of the wet coal dust layer, the force chain identification criterion is established and quantitative analysis of the force chain characteristics is carried out"},{"source_id":"K060126bd81e39251","relation":"irrelevant","reason":"Suspension-bridge shape-finding and finite-element model calibration (loop adjustment, temperature correction, pylon settlement, cable-saddle precession). No snap-through/limit-point criterion under spring loading, no stiffness-ratio condition, no Preisach/play operator content, and no evidence about the pair_A/pair_B driving spring or mounting length.","quote":"a nonlinear finite element model of the bridge was established and calibrated, taking into account factors such as pylon settlement and cable saddle precession"},{"source_id":"K71826186441ec4d5","relation":"irrelevant","reason":"The Maxwell criterion here is the lattice stretching/bending-dominated stiffness (rigidity) count for architected materials, not a limit-point or snap-through stability criterion.
